poincare.label: $r = \beta/2$
caption: The plane of $t$ and $\xi$ ($r = \beta/2$, $x = 0$) at $L = \beta$, drawn with $\xi$ across and $ct$ up. On it the metric is $-(L^2/r^2)\left(2c\,dt\,d\xi + (\beta^2/r^2)\,c^2dt^2\right)$, so one edge of every cone runs along $\xi$ at one $t$, and the other leans back with $d\xi = -(\beta^2/2r^2)\,c\,dt = -2\,c\,dt$. The nearer the boundary $r = 0$, the wider the cone, which opens there to the whole half plane after its $t$.

The rays along $\xi$ are null geodesics on which $t$ stands still. The curves moving left are null curves of the plane: light launched along one is turned toward larger $r$, away from the boundary, $\ddot{r} = (\beta^2/r^3)\,\dot{t}^2$.

global.label: $R = \beta/2$
caption: The plane of $T$ and $V$ ($R = \beta/2$, $X = 0$) at $L = \beta$ and $\omega = c/\beta$, drawn with $V$ across and $cT$ up. On it the metric is $-(L^2/R^2)\left(2c\,dT\,dV + (\beta^2/R^2 + \omega^2R^2/c^2)\,c^2dT^2\right)$, so one edge of every cone runs along $V$ at one $T$, and the other leans back with $dV = -\tfrac{1}{2}(\beta^2/R^2 + \omega^2R^2/c^2)\,c\,dT = -\tfrac{17}{8}\,c\,dT$. The trap widens the cone again far from the boundary, and the cone is narrowest at $R^2 = \beta c/\omega$, which is $R = \beta$ here.

The rays along $V$ are null geodesics on which $T$ stands still. The curves moving left are null curves of the plane: light launched along one is turned toward larger $R$, $\ddot{R} = (\beta^2/R^3 - \omega^2R/c^2)\,\dot{T}^2$, which is positive here.

global.label: $R = \beta$
caption: The plane of $T$ and $V$ ($R = \beta$, $X = 0$) at $L = \beta$ and $\omega = c/\beta$, drawn with $V$ across and $cT$ up. On it the metric is $-(L^2/R^2)\left(2c\,dT\,dV + (\beta^2/R^2 + \omega^2R^2/c^2)\,c^2dT^2\right)$, so one edge of every cone runs along $V$ at one $T$, and the other leans back with $dV = -\tfrac{1}{2}(\beta^2/R^2 + \omega^2R^2/c^2)\,c\,dT = -1\,c\,dT$. The trap widens the cone again far from the boundary, and the cone is narrowest at $R^2 = \beta c/\omega$, which is $R = \beta$ here.

The rays along $V$ are null geodesics on which $T$ stands still. At this depth the curves moving left are null geodesics too, since $\ddot{R} = (\beta^2/R^3 - \omega^2R/c^2)\,\dot{T}^2$ vanishes at $R^2 = \beta c/\omega$: light launched along one keeps its depth at the bottom of the trap.

global.label: $R = 2\beta$
caption: The plane of $T$ and $V$ ($R = 2\beta$, $X = 0$) at $L = \beta$ and $\omega = c/\beta$, drawn with $V$ across and $cT$ up. On it the metric is $-(L^2/R^2)\left(2c\,dT\,dV + (\beta^2/R^2 + \omega^2R^2/c^2)\,c^2dT^2\right)$, so one edge of every cone runs along $V$ at one $T$, and the other leans back with $dV = -\tfrac{1}{2}(\beta^2/R^2 + \omega^2R^2/c^2)\,c\,dT = -\tfrac{17}{8}\,c\,dT$. The trap widens the cone again far from the boundary, and the cone is narrowest at $R^2 = \beta c/\omega$, which is $R = \beta$ here.

The rays along $V$ are null geodesics on which $T$ stands still. The curves moving left are null curves of the plane: light launched along one is turned toward smaller $R$, $\ddot{R} = (\beta^2/R^3 - \omega^2R/c^2)\,\dot{T}^2$, which is negative here, back toward the bottom of the trap at $R = \beta$.

dynamical_exponent.label: $z = 1$
caption: The plane of $t$ and $\xi$ ($r = \beta/\sqrt{2}$, $x = 0$) for the dynamical exponent $z = 1$ at $L = \beta$, drawn with $\xi$ across and $ct$ up. On it the metric is $-(L^2/r^2)\left(2c\,dt\,d\xi + h\,c^2dt^2\right)$, so one edge of every cone runs along $\xi$ at one $t$, and the other leans back with $d\xi = -\tfrac{1}{2}h\,c\,dt = -\tfrac{1}{2}\,c\,dt$, where $h = (\beta/r)^{2z - 2} = 1$. This is anti-de Sitter space, where the cone is the same at every depth.
The rays along $\xi$ are null geodesics on which $t$ stands still. The curves moving left are null geodesics as well.

dynamical_exponent.label: $z = 3/2$
caption: The plane of $t$ and $\xi$ ($r = \beta/\sqrt{2}$, $x = 0$) for the dynamical exponent $z = 3/2$ at $L = \beta$, drawn with $\xi$ across and $ct$ up. On it the metric is $-(L^2/r^2)\left(2c\,dt\,d\xi + h\,c^2dt^2\right)$, so one edge of every cone runs along $\xi$ at one $t$, and the other leans back with $d\xi = -\tfrac{1}{2}h\,c\,dt = -\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\,c\,dt$, where $h = (\beta/r)^{2z - 2} = \sqrt{2}$. The cone is wider than anti-de Sitter's and narrower than Schrödinger spacetime's at the same depth.

The rays along $\xi$ are null geodesics on which $t$ stands still. The curves moving left are null curves of the plane: light launched along one is turned toward larger $r$, $\ddot{r} = (z - 1)(h/r)\,\dot{t}^2$.

global.label: light in the trap
legend: light launched from $R_0 = \beta$, the bottom of the trap, which keeps its depth
the edges of the Poincaré chart, $\omega T = \pm\pi/2$
caption: The surface $X = 0$ of the global chart seen from the side, $V$ left out, with $cT$ across and $R$ up, in units of $\beta$ ($L = \beta$, $\omega = c/\beta$). Each curve is a null geodesic launched at $T = 0$ from the depth $R_0$ with $\dot{R} = 0$, along the curve moving left of the plane of $T$ and $V$ there. The trap turns it back: its depth swings between $R_0$ and $\beta^2/R_0$ as $R^2 = R_0^2\cos^2\omega T + (\beta^4/R_0^2)\sin^2\omega T$, once in every $\pi/\omega$ of $T$, and the ray launched at $R_0 = \beta$ keeps its depth.

No ray reaches the boundary $R = 0$. The dashed lines are $\omega T = \pm\pi/2$, the edges of the Poincaré chart, whose $t = \tan(\omega T)/\omega$ and $r = R/\cos\omega T$ both run to infinity there: a ray leaves that chart at a finite value of its affine parameter, and in the global chart it swings on.
